title: Spec check on a single-slice launch

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The spec check runs only at wave launch. The daemon method `spec.check` is called by `l` in Waves (`internal/tui/waves.go:388`, `internal/tui/speccheck.go:62-78`) and by `ork wave start` (`internal/cli/wave.go:160,238-296`). `ork run` never calls it: `runSlice` goes from the plan to `run.start` (`internal/cli/run.go:107-135`). The daemon refuses an item with open questions only inside `wave.start` (`specGate`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:637`, `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:339-363`), not on `run.start` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1076-1085`). So a one-off slice can start on a thin spec that a wave would have held.

Split on 2026-10-29: this slice is the daemon gate and `ork run`. The Roadmap launch (the TUI sitting between the plan and the confirmation) is S184, which runs after this slice and after S166.

Parity row: 1.2 (check that a spec is ready) and gap 2 of the prioritized list in `docs/orchestrator-parity.md` (from S165).

Owner decisions that apply:
- The spec check is one read-only pass of the spec-check role; it asks structured questions, the owner answers in one sitting, ork appends an `Owner decisions (date)` paragraph with `slicer edit --append` and files keyed questions in adj only when the project has adj and the owner turned filing on (adj 164 roles.spec-check; `docs/design.md:188-212`). Spec check verdicts are an in-memory job cache tied to a fingerprint of the spec; ork stores no verdict (`docs/boundaries.md:18`).
- If the spec check itself fails (no Spec check row in the matrix, or the vendor fails), the launch is blocked, as `ork wave start` does today. There is no skip flag (owner, 2026-10-29).
- ork calls the slicer CLI for the row (`slicer relay-roles`, rule "Spec check row (rNN)") and for `edit`; it reimplements nothing (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:89-124`).
- The role is read-only and edits nothing; filling a thin spec is S179 (v1.1), not this slice.

Slicer check (`slicer find "spec check" --root ../slicer`): slicer provides the matrix row and the `edit --append` command (s392, s399, s400, all done); it has no launch-time check. ork already calls them for waves; this slice only adds the call to `ork run` and the daemon gate.

Cost to note: one spec-check role run per unchecked or changed spec, as for a wave. An item already checked and unchanged is answered from the daemon cache at no cost (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:166-171`).

Design (*proposed*): the check runs after the plan and before the start confirmation, the same place as in a wave. `ork run` prints the sitting on stdin and stdout (stderr with `--json`). An item whose questions stay open is held: `ork run` exits 1 with `held`. The daemon also refuses `run.start` for an item whose current spec has open questions (`spec_questions`), so a script cannot skip the check by calling the wire. The Roadmap launch gets the same sitting in S184.

Not in this slice: the Roadmap launch sitting (S184), filling or drafting a spec (S179), a flag or key that skips the check, changing the spec-check prompt or its lineup, the wave path.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestRunStartRefusesAnItemWithOpenSpecQuestions` (`internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`): after a check that left questions, `run.start` for that item returns code `spec_questions` and starts nothing.
- `TestRunStartDoesNotRefuseAnItemNeverChecked`: an unchecked item, or one whose spec changed since the check, still starts, as `specGate` allows for waves.
- `TestSingleRunCarriesSpecAnswersIntoTheBrief`: answers recorded by `spec.answer` reach the single run's implementer brief and run record (`decisions`).
- `TestRunCallsTheSpecCheckAfterThePlanAndBeforeConfirmation` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): call order is `run.plan`, `spec.check`, the confirmation, `run.start`; `--yes` still calls `spec.check`.
- `TestRunAsksSpecQuestionsOnStdinThenStarts`: a number picks an option, text is the answer, `spec.answer` gets the answers, and `run.start` follows.
- `TestRunHoldsAnItemWhoseQuestionsStayOpen`: an empty line or end of input exits 1, prints `held: S1 has N open spec questions`, and never calls `run.start`.
- `TestRunSpecCheckErrorStopsBeforeStart`: a `spec.check` error (for example no Spec check row) exits 1 with the code and message, and never calls `run.start`.
- `TestRunJSONKeepsTheSittingOffStdout`: with `--json` the questions go to stderr, stdout is one value, and a held item prints `{"started":false,"held":["S1"]}`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
UI slice: UI pass (r14), because `ork run` output changes (`internal/cli` output). No `internal/tui` change and no golden view in this slice. Test-first: write the tests above; the existing `run` tests will also fail until their stubs answer `spec.check`. Then:
1. `internal/daemon/runs.go:1076-1085`: in `handleRun`, before `d.startRun` for `MethodRunStart`, call `d.specGate(ctx, p.Project, p.Item)` (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:339`). `startWave` keeps its own gate (`:637`), which gives the per-item error; the single path gets it here, so the gate runs once on each path. No new wire method.
2. `internal/cli/run.go`: after the plan is printed (`:113-119`) and before the confirmation (`:120`), call the existing `a.specCheck(ctx, o, reader, prompts, &daemon.WaveStartParams{Items: []daemon.RunParams{params}})` (`internal/cli/wave.go:238`). If it returns no item, print `held`, and exit `ExitFailure`; with `--json` print `{"started":false,"held":[ITEM]}` as `wave.go:169` does. A non-zero code from it is returned as is. Move `specCheck` and `askSpecQuestions` to `internal/cli/speccheck.go` (new) only if that keeps `wave.go` readable; no logic change.
3. Existing stubs: make `runPrompted` (`internal/cli/run_test.go:35-44`) and the `Call` stubs in `TestRunShowsPlanBeforeConfirmation` and `TestRunYesStartsAndOwnerCommands` answer `spec.check` with `{"items":[{"item":"S1","ready":true}]}`.
4. Docs: `docs/design.md:186-200` (the check also runs on `ork run`, and `run.start` refuses an item with open questions) and `:974-996` (`ork run` prints the sitting and holds an item), `docs/guide.md` sections 7 and 9 (S165) for `ork run`. S184 adds the Roadmap launch text to `docs/design.md:186-212`; merge main before the gate if it landed first.
Order: independent of S166 for the code, but S184 needs this slice (the daemon gate) and S166. S168 and S169 do not touch these paths.
